were characterized by the presence of only one imaginary
frequency, which is further verified by performing the intrinsic
reaction coordinate (IRC) analysis.34 Solvent effects (benzene)
were incorporated using the solvation model based on density
(SMD).35 To investigate the ligand properties and bonding
situation of the studied molecules, natural bond orbital (NBO)
analysis was performed on the optimized geometries.36 To
check the reliability of the calculated adiabatic ΔES−T values,
we have recalculated them using two different functionals
(B3PW9137 and ωB97XD38). Dispersion effects were included
using the D3BJ version of Grimme’s dispersion correction in
combination with the original D3 damping function using the
keyword empiricaldispersion = GD3BJ.39 Furthermore, to
check the presence of any internal instability in the proposed
silylenes, we have performed a stability check on the single-
determinant wave functions of the optimized singlet state
geometries.40,41 The energetics for all of the reactions has been
computed in terms of change in Gibbs free energies at 298 K
and 1 atm pressure using the Gaussian 09 suite of programs.42
■RESULTS AND DISCUSSION
The important geometrical and electronic parameters of the
optimized singlet state geometries of 1−6, as well as those of
the truncated versions of the synthetically attainable silylenes
V, VIII, and IX (V′, VIII′, and IX′, respectively, where the
bulky Dipp and adamantly groups were replaced with a phenyl
group), are presented in Table 1. The computed geometrical
parameters of V′, VIII′, and IX′ are in excellent agreement
with the observed values, thereby lending credence to the level
of theory used for the present study. Replacement of the
tetracoordinated quaternary carbon adjacent to the amino
group in 1 by BNMe2 (2), silicon (3), and carbonyl group (4)
led to an increase in the Si−N bond distance (r2), which may
be attributed to the delocalization of the amino lone pair (NLP)
not only to the formally vacant p orbital of the central Si but
also to the empty 2p and 3p orbitals at boron (2) and silicon
(3), respectively, as well as the π*CO orbital (4). Annulation at
the position α to the silicon center in 5 and 6 led to a dramatic
increase in Si−N bond lengths compared to that in 1.
The thermodynamic stability of the divalent group 14
compounds can be judged from an evaluation of their singlet−
triplet energy gaps (ΔES−T).43 All the proposed system
possesses reasonable ΔES−T values ranging from 27.1 to 41.3
kcal mol−1, with the lowest being computed for annulated
silylene 5 (Figure 1). The presence of an annulated quinine
moiety leads to destabilization of the singlet state via
withdrawal of the π-electron density from NLP, thus resulting
in a lower ΔES−T values for 5 and 6.44 The reliability of the
calculated ΔES−T values were checked by recalculating them
using other functionals and obtained comparable results
(Table S1). The ligand properties of the proposed silylenes
(Scheme 2) can be understood by studying the nature and
energies of the frontier molecular orbitals. It is evident from
Figure 1 that the installation of the carbonyl group or
annulation led to a substantial increase in the accepting ability
of the silylene center. It is worth mentioning that except for 1,
all of the proposed CAASis show better accepting ability than
experimental systems V′, VIII′, and IX′. The σ-donation
ability of 4, 5, and 6 decreases significantly in comparison to 1,
which may be attributed to the incorporation of the carbonyl
group in 4 and annulation in the ring framework of 5 and 6.
From the above discussion, it is evident that the proposed six-
membered CAASis possess better ligand properties in
comparison to experimental systems V′, VIII′, and IX′. Such
enhanced ligand properties render them potential candidates
for small molecule activations. We sought to investigate such
activations by considering H2 and C2H2 as substrates together
with the dehydrogenation of ammonia borane in our present
study. To make the study relevant to the synthetic chemists,
the energetics of the activations was compared with isolable
and experimentally evaluated systems.
Activation of Dihydrogen and Acetylene
Several industrially relevant chemical transformations involve
the splitting of enthalpically strong bonds such as H−H, C−H,
etc., which has mostly been accomplished employing
transition-metal (TM) catalysts that are both expensive and
toxic.45,46 On the contrary to TMs, the main-group elements
are cost-effective and environmentally benign, and hence,
efforts were made to synthesize main-group-based catalysts as
alternatives for TMs. In 2005, Power and co-workers for the
first time reported the activation of H2 by using a digermyne
complex under ambient reaction conditions.47 In a seminal
work, Bertrand and co-workers reported the metal-free single-
site activation of H2 and NH3 by both acyclic and cyclic
carbenes.48 In 2012, Aldridge, Jones, and Mountford reported
the facile splitting of dihydrogen by mixed amido boryl acyclic
silylene.49 Later, several other acyclic silylenes were isolated
that could cleave the H−H bond of dihydrogen.50 In 2008,
Driess’s group reported C−H insertion and cycloaddition by V
(Scheme 1).51 Inspired by these and other reports of metal-
free activation of small molecules, we decided to probe the
potential of the proposed silylenes (Scheme 2) toward such
bond activations.
The most important and dominant interaction for H2
activation is that between the σ-symmetric donor orbital of

thereby elongating and polarizing the H−H bond, as shown in
Figure 2, by considering 1 as the representative silylene. The
electronic and geometrical changes that took place as a result

4. Computational Methods and Results 
4.1 Computational Methods 
All the calculations were performed on the Gaussian 16 (A.03) program package.[15] 
Considering the applicability of PBE0 functional on computing the energy barriers of 
organic and organometallic reactions in solution,[16] the hybrid PBE0[17] functional in 
conjugation with the def2-SVP basis set[18] and the D3 version of Grimme’s dispersion 
correction with Becke-Johnson damping (GD3-BJ)[19] was used for structure 
optimization. The corresponding frequency analysis at the same level was conducted to 
characterize the nature of the optimized structures; i.e., energy minimums without 
imaginary frequencies or transition states with only one imaginary frequency; and the 
imaginary model connects the initial and the final states. On the basis of 
PBE0(GD3BJ)/def2-SVP-optimized geometries, MN15 functional[20] in conjugation 
with the def2-TZVP basis set were used to calculate the self-consistent reaction field 
(SCRF) single-point energies in the solvation of N,N-dmethylacetamide (MN15-
SCRF(SCRF)/def2-TZVP//PBE0/def2-SVP) by using the SMD solvation model.[21] 
Graphics with 3D rending in ball-and-stick model was drawn in CYLview 1.0 
visualization software.[22] The spin density on INT-C was analyzed by the wavefunction 
analysis program Multiwfn 3.8.[23]
source.S12_claim:
S12 
 
required more free-energy input than the photo-excitation of silyl palladium hydride 
complex INT-A from the singlet to the triplet state. The decomposition of silyl 
palladium hydride complex INT-A-triplet to silyl radical PhH2Si and the monovalent 
palladium hydride complex Pd(I)H-XantPhos is endothermic by 12.4 kcal/mol. The 
computational result suggests that the hydrogen atom transfer from the aryl radical INT-
E to the monovalent palladium hydride complex Pd(I)H-XantPhos can proceed facile 
with a negative energy barrier and the hydrogen evolution through the reductive 
elimination of the palladium dihydride complex INT-G only needs to overcome a free-
energy barrier of 0.9 kcal/mol. The other reaction path through the direct reaction of 
photoexcited Pd(0) species with the benzotriazole substrate 1a via SET, generating Pd(I) 
and a radical anion (INT-H), was also computed. Compared with the path of silyl 
radical-mediated reaction, the Pd(I)-activated ring-opening C–N bond cleavage of 
benzotriazole in this reaction path (INT-H → INT-I via TS7) has to surmount a higher 
free-energy barrier. Moreover, the position of ring-opening C–N bond cleavage 
transition state TS7 on the potential energy surface was higher than the position of both 
photoexcited Pd(0) species Pd-Xantphos-triplet and the silyl-mediated ring-opening 
C–N bond cleavage transition state TS2. These energetic patterns suggested the reaction 
path via the direct SET from the photoexcited Pd(0) species to the benzotriazole 
substrate was much less plausible than the silyl radical-mediated reaction path. The 
computational investigation also surveyed the plausibility of the reaction path starting 
from the hydrogen atom abstracting from PhSiH3 by the photo-excited benzotriazole 
1a in the absence of the palladium catalyst (Figure S7). The computational results show 
that this path has to undergo the transition states with much higher free energy than the 
other two paths shown in Figure S4.

report.limitations: The systems are isolated neutral species/ion pairs in a CPCM acetonitrile continuum; no explicit-solvent, thermal or condensed-phase sampling was performed. Ion-pair coverage is finite and TFAP yielded one distinct start. Selected structures have only very small residual imaginary modes (<16 cm^-1), not strictly all-real Hessians. Mulliken charges are basis- and geometry-sensitive observables, as directly demonstrated here; Loewdin values are an auxiliary partitioning check and do not replace the requested Mulliken quantities.

report.hypothesis: A plausible inductive/electrostatic explanation is that the hydroperoxide-bearing substituent in (R)-4 produces a larger molecular electrostatic polarization and strongly differentiates the hydroperoxide-proximal alkene carbon from the distal carbon, whereas the chemically equivalent alkene sites in 7 remain nearly unpolarized.
report.hypothesis_test: The global electrostatic part is supported: the SMD-water dipole magnitude is 5.221617 D for (R)-4 and 2.222782 D for 7. The proposed strong local C=C polarization is not supported by the consistently computed Loewdin charges. For (R)-4, q(C2)-q(C4) is -0.003482 e; for 7, q(C8)-q(C10) is -0.001905 e. Thus (R)-4 has only 0.001577 e more absolute within-bond charge separation than 7, and its proximal carbon is slightly more negative rather than more positive. validation.protocol: Every advanced candidate was optimized at GFN2-xTB/tight with charge 0 and multiplicity 1, then evaluated with an xTB Hessian and nonlinear vibrational analysis. A minimum was accepted when no imaginary frequency exceeded 10 cm^-1; sub-0.1 cm^-1 raw imaginary values were treated as numerical translations/rotations. RRHO G used 298.15 K, 101325 Pa, symmetry number 1 and spin 0. One relaxed mapped conformer per symmetry-unique connectivity was compared. Intended new bonds were checked by mapped distances and GFN2-xTB Wiberg orders; carbon best-plane RMS was a separate structural discriminator.
validation.process_evidence: P0, M1, M2, B1 and B2 all converged and all have zero imaginary modes above 10 cm^-1. P0 itself has G=-2042.261723949 eV, Eel=-75.403548203 Eh, largest raw imaginary 0.0210 cm^-1 and carbon-plane RMS 0.6772 A (structure art_64ecde9dd366490699839b11f771a284; Hessian art_cf5dc77a5a114fd681bc5ad17d499338; frequencies art_84879e7e8fd54e4bb962eca0eda24178; thermochemistry art_2d94d88d51d74cc5b0d6e8c3a69b1253). Full joined metrics are in outputs/execution_jobs/job_b523b3ec4d1f4e25a98812293b4b3370/outputs/evidence_summary.json and candidate_metrics.csv.

comparison.quantity: Within-formula 298.15 K, 1 atm ideal-gas RRHO relative Gibbs free energy (single-conformer GFN2-xTB), with equal-formula electronic-energy, Wiberg-bond-order and planarity checks.
comparison.ordering_or_result: First stage: M2 (0.0) < M1 (19.63 kJ mol^-1), a modest preference comparable to the 15 kJ mol^-1 screening uncertainty. Bis products: B1 (0.0) << B2 (229.08 kJ mol^-1), a decisive final-connectivity preference. B1 is also much more planar (0.2755 versus 0.9596 A carbon RMS).
comparison.electronic_evidence: Electronic energies give the same ordering: M2 below M1 by 17.15 kJ mol^-1 and B1 below B2 by 232.90 kJ mol^-1. All intended bonds remain covalent after relaxation (lengths 1.4376-1.4580 A; Wiberg orders 1.035-1.195).

report.conclusion: The endpoint evidence supports the symmetry-unique sequential M1 -> B1 bis-Mallory connectivity (new precursor bonds C3-C51 and C21-C41, with the stated symmetry-equivalent orbit) as the selected bis product. M2 is a genuine and slightly lower-free-energy mono minimum, so a competing first closure cannot be excluded at this screening level; however, its sequential B2 continuation is disfavored by 229.08 +/- 15 kJ mol^-1 and is far more nonplanar. B2 is therefore a structurally valid but thermodynamically unsupported selected endpoint. This is an isolated-molecule ground-state endpoint/connectivity conclusion, not a rate or excited-state-dynamics claim.

coverage.generation_rule: Infer the C-C graph from the supplied geometry using C-C <=1.95 A and assign each H to its nearest C below 1.60 A. Generate a first-stage Mallory closure for every pair of nonbonded H-bearing carbons separated by exactly five C-C graph edges, add that bond and delete the two attached H atoms. Retain precursor-accessible pairs with reacting-carbon separation <=4.30 A. Generate sequential bis channels as unordered, H-disjoint pairs of retained closures. Remove equivalent retained mono and bis connectivities under the eight automorphisms of the inferred labeled-element graph.
coverage.searched_scope: Twenty topological first-stage hypotheses were generated. Sixteen were recorded individually and discarded by the fixed distance rule. Four accessible raw closures collapsed to two mono orbits (M1 orbit size 3, M2 orbit size 1). Four raw disjoint closure pairs collapsed to two bis orbits (B1 and B2, each orbit size 2). Both retained mono and both retained bis representatives were optimized, frequency-validated, thermochemically compared and bond-order checked; there were no failed or unresolved advanced calculations.
coverage.unresolved_scope: No retained connectivity is unresolved. The finite search is conditioned on the supplied displaced cis conformer, the 4.30 A accessibility cutoff, and one relaxed conformer per unique connectivity; transition states and excited-state kinetics were outside the requested boundary.
coverage.stopping_statement: Stopped after exhaustive application of the declared graph/distance rule, automorphism deduplication, and complete validation of every retained unique mono and bis channel.

search_and_validation.candidate_generation: A finite CREST/GFN2-xTB conformer search of neutral singlet 3a retained 21 structures within 8 kcal/mol. Without presupposing a TS geometry, candidates were ranked independently for the two allowed bond-reorganization hypotheses: cleavage of C1-C2 with formation of C10-C13 for [3,3], or formation of C16-C20 for [5,5]. The two closest unique geometries per channel were advanced: CREST-06/15 for [3,3] and CREST-13/09 for [5,5]. Each underwent an explicit relaxed forming-bond scan from its starting separation to 1.55 A (19 points for each [3,3] scan; 31 and 33 points for [5,5]), and each interior maximum seeded a TS search.
search_and_validation.deduplication: Energy-ordered conformers were treated as duplicates when their no-reflection, Kabsch-aligned heavy-atom RMSD was <0.25 A. This reduced 21 CREST frames to 18 unique identities; CREST-11, -18, and -21 mapped to CREST-10, -17, and -20, respectively.
search_and_validation.coverage: The conformer ensemble contained 21 structures within the declared 8 kcal/mol window (18 unique). Four independent channel/conformer scans completed: [3,3]/CREST-06 (maximum 2.1419 A, rise 13.2823 kcal/mol), [3,3]/CREST-15 (2.1464 A, 12.5061), [5,5]/CREST-13 (2.0565 A, 12.7318), and [5,5]/CREST-09 (1.9591 A, 16.5392). Three pysisyphus TS branches failed its convergence criteria at 150 cycles; Sella recovery validated both [3,3] branches, while the original pysisyphus search validated [5,5]/CREST-13. The chosen [3,3] TS is the lower-G of two independently validated conformer-derived TSs; one validated [5,5] TS plus one documented failed independent branch defines that channel's finite coverage.
search_and_validation.stopping_rule: Stop after two distinct low-forming-distance seeds per channel had converged scans and at least one fully converged, one-imaginary-frequency, connectivity-validated TS per channel; compare all validated TS Gibbs energies and retain the lowest for each channel.
search_and_validation.limitations: These are internally consistent semiempirical GFN2-xTB/RRHO barriers, not DFT or coupled-cluster benchmarks. Harmonic RRHO and symmetry number 1 were used; no hindered-rotor or conformer-population correction was added. The finite search cannot prove absence of a still lower unsampled TS conformer.

report.conclusion: At the disclosed GFN2-xTB/RRHO level, the validated 298.15 K barriers relative to the lowest located conformer of 3a are 13.9518 kcal/mol for [3,3] and 16.4730 kcal/mol for [5,5]. Thus [3,3] is favored by 2.5211 kcal/mol. Both assignments are supported by converged first-order saddle points, exactly one significant imaginary frequency, channel-specific opposing bond motion, bidirectional IRC descent, and converged endpoint minima with the expected bond connectivity.
